register: Plain tu, neutral US Spanish, short sentences. Product names stay in English with their English article: The Forge, The Refinery, t.ROY. Documents stay English this pass.
how_to_use: status=locked entries are enforced by lib/__tests__/i18n-termbase.test.ts: no Spanish catalog value may match an avoid pattern. status=proposed entries are machine suggestions that wait for a bilingual reader; they are not enforced. Add an entry when a back-translation check or a reader finds a recurring problem.

terms.note: "antecedentes" alone can read as work background. Found in 16 back-translation flags on 2026-11-13. Work history is "historial laboral". Exception (2026-11-14): "verificación(es) de antecedentes" is the ordinary Spanish for a background check and is allowed as that exact phrase; do NOT write "verificación de antecedentes penales" for a plain background check, which narrows it to a criminal-record check (a job-title mismatch is caught by an employment check).

terms.es: borrar los datos de esta computadora
terms.note: The button erases saved work and signs the person out. "Limpiar" reads like cleaning the machine and "borrar esta computadora" like erasing the machine. Say what is erased: the data on it.
Back-translation found it rendered as Completa. Normal is the same word in both languages.

Troy 2026-11-14: "lugar" for a Refinery seat (tentative, "idk i guess lugar"); a bilingual reader should confirm. "cupo" stays only where Spanish means an allowance or quota (AI allowance: "tu cupo de IA"). Not enforced by a test because the word is ordinary.
"socio" reads as a business partner or spouse. Proposed by the comparison pass.
"centro" alone does not say jail or prison. Applied in the record-choice screen; confirm wording and region with a reader.
"por encargo" was flagged as unclear. A native reader should pick the everyday word.
"gestor de casos" versus "administrador de casos". Reader should choose what reentry programs actually say.
Not "verificación de antecedentes penales" unless the English says criminal background check.

Never "eliminar" or "borrar" for record relief: it reads as a guaranteed erasure, and sealed or expunged records can still be seen by some agencies. Keep the English legal term in parentheses so a person can look it up. "Eliminar/borrar" stays correct for deleting a person's own data in the product.

The Refinery's private document store (/dashboard/documents). Capital V in English, Bóveda in Spanish. The resume library (/dashboard/vault, shown as My resumes) is never called the Vault. Machine suggestion, waiting for a bilingual reader.
